ru.L: вот, {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} посылаю и возьму все племена севера, — слово {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}, — и [пошлю] к Навуходорносору, царю Вавилона, {{deity_pronoun:моему|Моему}} рабу, и приведу их на эту землю, и на её жителей, и на все эти народы вокруг; и предам их заклятию, и сделаю их ужасом, и посмеянием, и вечными развалинами.
ru.B: Я пошлю за всеми племенами севера, говорит {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}, и за Навуходорносором, царём Вавилона, {{deity_pronoun:моим|Моим}} рабом. Я приведу их на эту землю и на её жителей и на все народы вокруг неё. Я предам их заклятию и сделаю их ужасом, предметом насмешек и вечными развалинами.
ru.R: Я пошлю за всеми народами севера, говорит {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}. Я пошлю за {{deity_pronoun:моим|Моим}} рабом Навуходорносором, царём Вавилона. Я приведу их, чтобы они напали на эту землю, на людей, которые здесь живут, и на все народы вокруг. Я полностью уничтожу их всех. Люди будут ужасаться, глядя на них, и смеяться над ними. Эти места навсегда останутся в развалинах.

ja.L: 見なさい、わたしは人を遣わして、北のすべての氏族を連れて来る――{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の言葉――。また、わたしのしもべ、バビロンの王ネブカドネツァルのもとに[人を遣わす]。わたしは彼らを、この地とその住民と、周りのこれらすべての国々に攻め来させ、それらを滅ぼし尽くし、それらを恐怖とし、あざけりの口笛とし、とこしえの廃墟とする。
ja.B: わたしは、北のすべての民と、わたしのしもべ、バビロンの王ネブカドネツァルを呼び寄せる、と{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}は告げる。わたしは彼らに、この地とその住民と、周りのすべての国々を攻めさせる。わたしはそれらを滅ぼし尽くし、恐怖とあざけりの的とし、とこしえの廃墟とする。
ja.R: わたしは、北のすべての民を呼び寄せる、と{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}は言う。わたしのしもべ、バビロンの王ネブカドネツァルを呼び寄せる。わたしは彼らに、この地と、ここに住む人々と、周りのすべての国々を攻めさせる。わたしはそれらをすっかり滅ぼす。人々はそれを見て震え上がり、あざける。それらの地は、いつまでも廃墟のままになる。

uk.L: ось {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} посилаю і візьму всі роди півночі, говорить {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}, і [посилаю] до Навуходоносора, царя Вавилону, {{deity_pronoun:мого|Мого}} раба, і приведу їх на цей край, і на його мешканців, і на всі ці народи довкола; і віддам їх на закляття, і зроблю їх жахом, і посвистом, і вічними руїнами.
uk.B: Я пошлю по всі народи півночі, говорить {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}, і по Навуходоносора, царя Вавилону, {{deity_pronoun:мого|Мого}} раба. Я приведу їх на цей край і на його людей, і на всі народи довкола нього. Я віддам їх на повне знищення і зроблю їх жахом, предметом зневаги і вічними руїнами.
uk.R: Я пошлю по всі народи з півночі, каже {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}. Я пошлю по {{deity_pronoun:мого|Мого}} раба Навуходоносора, царя Вавилону. Я приведу їх, щоб вони напали на цей край і на людей, які тут живуть, і на всі народи довкола вас. Я цілком знищу їх усіх. Люди жахатимуться їх і глузуватимуть з них. Ті місця навіки лежатимуть у руїнах.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar ... my servant: the foreign king is God's instrument, carrying out God's purpose
alternatives: my servant meaning a worshiper of God
decisions.reason: God calls the king of Babylon "my servant" here and in 27:6 and 43:10. The title does not mean that Nebuchadrezzar worshiped Israel's God or was good. It means that he did God's work, the way a servant carries out his master's orders: he would bring the judgment God had decreed. Isaiah says something similar of Assyria as the rod of God's anger (Isaiah 10:5-7) and of Cyrus as God's anointed (Isaiah 45:1). The title also tells Judah that resisting Babylon is resisting God (27:6-8). The Greek translation lacks "Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon my servant" here (see the note at 1:1; this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: all the clans of the north: the peoples who make up the army from the north
decisions.reason: The enemy from the north was announced in Jeremiah's call (1:14-15, where the same clans are named) and in the poems of chapters 4-6 (4:6; 6:22). Here, for the first time, that enemy is named: Babylon and its allies.

decisions.choice: devote them to destruction: give them over wholly to destruction as under God's ban
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for the ban, the total destruction of what is given over to God (Deuteronomy 7:2; Joshua 6:21). What Israel once did to the nations of Canaan God now does to Judah and its neighbors.

decisions.choice: a horror and a hissing: a sight that appalls, at which people whistle in shock and scorn
decisions.reason: As in 19:8. Hissing or whistling at a ruin showed shock and contempt (18:16; 1 Kings 9:8). "Everlasting ruins" means ruins that will stand for a very long time.

decisions.choice: servant (every level)
decisions.reason: The style guide gives "slave" at Literal for this word. Here, as in Isaiah, the word names one who carries out God's purpose (see m1), and Jeremiah uses the same title for God's prophets (verse 4), so "servant" is kept at every level. "Slave" would suggest that the point is the king's lowly status, when the point is the task God has given him.

decisions.choice: devote to destruction (L, B), destroy completely (R); a horror and a hissing (L), a horror, an object of scorn (B), horrified ... mock (R)
decisions.reason: The set wording for the ban and for this list. Readable spells the list out in short sentences. Literal supplies "[I am sending]" and "[it]", which the Hebrew leaves understood.

decisions.choice: mi siervo
decisions.reason: Nebuchadrezzar is God's "siervo" at every level, the same word as for the prophets, so the reader sees that the foreign king serves God's purpose (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: los consagraré al exterminio (Literal); los destinaré a la destrucción (Balanced)
decisions.reason: *Herem* is giving over wholly to destruction under God's ban (meaning decision m3); Literal keeps the sense of consecration, Readable says "destruiré por completo".

decisions.choice: mtumishi wangu
decisions.reason: Nebukadreza is God's "mtumishi" at every level, as the English keeps "servant": the word says whose purpose he carries out (meaning decision m1). No deity span is used for him.

decisions.choice: "vouer à l'interdit" (L, B); "détruire complètement" (R)
decisions.reason: The ban (herem) as the published French books say it ("vouer à l'interdit"); Readable says what it means, as the English does. "Mon serviteur" for Nebuchadnezzar keeps "serviteur" at every level.

decisions.choice: "đầy tớ Ta" for Nebuchadrezzar
decisions.reason: The terms note's rule: God's servants are "đầy tớ" at every level, including Nebuchadrezzar "my servant" (25:9; 27:6), whom God uses as his instrument.

decisions.choice: "내 종 ... 느부갓레살"
decisions.reason: God calls the foreign king "my servant" (meaning decision m1); Korean keeps "종", the word used for God's servants the prophets, so the point is not lost.

decisions.choice: "진멸하다" for *heherim*
decisions.reason: "진멸" is the word for devoting to complete destruction under God's ban (meaning decision m3); Readable says "완전히 멸망시키다".

decisions.choice: o meu servo (every level); destinar à destruição (L, B), destruir completamente (R); um assobio (L), um objeto de zombaria (B)
decisions.reason: Nabucodorosor is God's instrument (m1), so "o meu servo" at every level, as the English keeps "servant" and Isaiah calls Cyrus "o meu pastor". The ban (m3) is "destinar à destruição" at Literal and Balanced, the wording of Isaiah 11:15 and the Law. The hissing (m4) keeps the words 18:16 sets for the book: "assobio" at Literal, the whistle of shock and scorn, and "objeto de zombaria" at Balanced.

decisions.choice: "ባሪያዬ" (Literal), "አገልጋዬ" (Balanced, Readable) for Nebuchadrezzar "my servant"
decisions.reason: The terms list's pair for ʿeved; the Babylonian king is God's instrument, which "አገልጋዬ" says without suggesting he was a slave bought and sold. The same pair is used in 27:6.

decisions.choice: "ማፏጫ" (hissing) at Literal; "መዘባበቻ" (object of scorn) at Balanced
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the whistle of shock and scorn; Balanced says what it means. The pair recurs in 25:18 and 29:18.

decisions.choice: "віддам на закляття" (L), "віддам на повне знищення" (B) for devoting to destruction
decisions.reason: L keeps the sense of a ban that hands a people over to God; B says plainly what it means.

decisions.choice: अपना दास नबूकदरेस्सर
decisions.reason: God calls the foreign king "my servant" (ʿavdi): दास at every level, as the terms note sets for ʿeved, so that the reader sees the same word God uses of the prophets in verse 4. The king is God's instrument here.

decisions.choice: सर्वनाश के लिए अर्पित करना (L, B); पूरी तरह नष्ट करना (R); सीटी का विषय (L), उपहास का विषय (B)
decisions.reason: The ban (herem) keeps the wording of 1 Kings 9:21 and 20:42 in this translation. The hissing is सीटी at Literal (the gesture of shock and scorn, as 2 Chronicles 29:8) and उपहास at Balanced, as the English has "an object of scorn".

decisions.choice: моим рабом
decisions.reason: Nebuchadrezzar is God's ʿeved, the one who carries out his purpose; Russian keeps "раб" at every level, as the notes set for this word, so that the same title is heard as for the prophets in verse 4.

decisions.choice: предам заклятию (L, B), полностью уничтожу (R); ужасом и посмеянием (L), предметом насмешек (B)
decisions.reason: The ban (ḥerem) takes the wording of Deuteronomy and Joshua. The "hissing" (whistling in shock and scorn) is given its sense, as 2 Chronicles 29:8 does; Readable says it in sentences.

decisions.choice: 'avdi of Nebuchadrezzar "わたしのしもべ" at every level (the JER rule for "my servant").
decisions.reason: m1: the foreign king as God's instrument; the word is the same title God gives his prophets, and the footnote says so.

decisions.choice: hecharamtim "滅ぼし尽くし" (L, B), "すっかり滅ぼす" (R); leshammah velishreqah "恐怖とし、あざけりの口笛とし" (L), "恐怖とあざけりの的" (B), as 18:16 and 19:8.
decisions.reason: m3, m4; the JER-3 forms for shammah and sheriqah.

source.text: וְהַאֲבַדְתִּ֣י מֵהֶ֗ם ק֤וֹל שָׂשׂוֹן֙ וְק֣וֹל שִׂמְחָ֔ה ק֥וֹל חָתָ֖ן וְק֣וֹל כַּלָּ֑ה ק֥וֹל רֵחַ֖יִם וְא֥וֹר נֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will make perish from them [the] sound of joy and [the] sound of gladness, [the] voice of bridegroom and [the] voice of bride, [the] sound of millstones and [the] light of lamp.

en.L: And I will banish from them the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstones and the light of the lamp.
en.B: I will take away from them the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of bridegroom and bride, the grinding of the millstones and the light of the lamp.
en.R: I will end the sounds of joy and happiness among them. No one will hear the happy voices of a bride and groom at their wedding. No one will hear the sound of grain being ground at the mill. No one will see the light of a lamp in their homes.

es.L: Y haré desaparecer de entre ellos la voz de gozo y la voz de alegría, la voz del novio y la voz de la novia, el ruido del molino y la luz de la lámpara.
es.B: Quitaré de en medio de ellos los sonidos de gozo y de alegría, las voces del novio y de la novia, el ruido de las piedras de moler y la luz de la lámpara.
es.R: Acabaré con los sonidos de gozo y felicidad entre ellos. Nadie oirá las voces alegres de los novios en su boda. Nadie oirá el ruido del grano al molerse en el molino. Nadie verá la luz de una lámpara en sus casas.

fr.L: Et je ferai disparaître du milieu d’eux le cri de joie et le cri d’allégresse, la voix du fiancé et la voix de la fiancée, le bruit des meules et la lumière de la lampe.
fr.B: Je ferai cesser chez eux les cris de joie et d’allégresse, les voix du fiancé et de la fiancée, le bruit des meules et la lumière de la lampe.
fr.R: Je ferai cesser chez eux les cris de joie et de bonheur. On n’entendra plus les voix joyeuses des mariés à leur mariage. On n’entendra plus le bruit du grain qu’on moud. On ne verra plus la lumière des lampes dans les maisons.

sw.L: Nami nitaondoa kwao sauti ya furaha na sauti ya shangwe, sauti ya bwana arusi na sauti ya bibi arusi, sauti ya mawe ya kusagia na nuru ya taa.
sw.B: Nitaziondoa kwao sauti za furaha na shangwe, sauti za bwana arusi na bibi arusi, mlio wa mawe ya kusagia na mwanga wa taa.
sw.R: Nitakomesha sauti za furaha na shangwe kati yao. Hakuna atakayesikia sauti za furaha za bibi arusi na bwana arusi harusini. Hakuna atakayesikia sauti ya nafaka ikisagwa kwa jiwe la kusagia. Hakuna atakayeona mwanga wa taa majumbani mwao.

vi.L: Ta sẽ làm cho tiêu mất khỏi giữa chúng tiếng vui mừng và tiếng hân hoan, tiếng chàng rể và tiếng cô dâu, tiếng cối xay và ánh sáng của đèn.
vi.B: Ta sẽ cất khỏi chúng tiếng vui mừng hân hoan, tiếng chàng rể và cô dâu, tiếng cối xay và ánh đèn.
vi.R: Ta sẽ chấm dứt những tiếng vui mừng hớn hở giữa chúng. Sẽ không ai còn nghe tiếng cười nói của cô dâu chú rể trong ngày cưới. Sẽ không ai còn nghe tiếng xay lúa nơi cối xay. Sẽ không ai còn thấy ánh đèn trong nhà.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 그들에게서 기뻐하는 소리와 즐거워하는 소리, 신랑의 목소리와 신부의 목소리, 맷돌 소리와 등불 빛을 없애겠다.
ko.B: 내가 그들에게서 기뻐하고 즐거워하는 소리, 신랑과 신부의 목소리, 맷돌 가는 소리와 등불 빛을 사라지게 하겠다.
ko.R: 내가 그들 가운데서 기쁘고 즐거운 소리가 그치게 하겠다. 결혼식에서 신랑 신부의 즐거운 목소리도 들리지 않을 것이다. 맷돌로 곡식을 가는 소리도 들리지 않을 것이다. 집집마다 켜 두던 등불 빛도 보이지 않을 것이다.

pt.L: E farei desaparecer do meio deles a voz de alegria e a voz de júbilo, a voz do noivo e a voz da noiva, o som das mós e a luz da lâmpada.
pt.B: Farei cessar entre eles os sons de alegria e de festa, as vozes do noivo e da noiva, o barulho das mós e a luz da lâmpada.
pt.R: Vou acabar com os sons de alegria e felicidade no meio deles. Ninguém vai ouvir as vozes felizes de um noivo e de uma noiva no seu casamento. Ninguém vai ouvir o barulho de grãos sendo moídos no moinho. Ninguém vai ver a luz de uma lâmpada nas casas.

am.L: ከእነርሱም የደስታን ድምፅና የሐሤትን ድምፅ፣ የሙሽራውን ድምፅና የሙሽራይቱን ድምፅ፣ የወፍጮውን ድምፅና የመብራቱን ብርሃን አጠፋለሁ።
am.B: የደስታንና የሐሤትን ድምፅ፣ የሙሽራውንና የሙሽራይቱን ድምፅ፣ የወፍጮውን ድምፅና የመብራቱን ብርሃን ከእነርሱ አስወግዳለሁ።
am.R: በመካከላቸው የደስታና የሐሤት ድምፅ እንዲያበቃ አደርጋለሁ። በሠርግ ላይ የሙሽራውና የሙሽራይቱ የደስታ ድምፅ ከእንግዲህ አይሰማም። እህል የሚፈጭበት የወፍጮ ድምፅ አይሰማም። በቤታቸውም የመብራት ብርሃን አይታይም።

hi.L: और मैं उनके बीच से हर्ष का शब्द और आनंद का शब्द, दूल्हे का शब्द और दुल्हन का शब्द, चक्की का शब्द और दीपक का उजियाला मिटा दूँगा।
hi.B: मैं उनके बीच से हर्ष और आनंद के स्वर, दूल्हे और दुल्हन के स्वर, चक्की की आवाज़ और दीपक का उजियाला मिटा दूँगा।
hi.R: मैं उनके बीच से ख़ुशी और आनंद की आवाज़ें बंद कर दूँगा। किसी विवाह में दूल्हे और दुल्हन की ख़ुशी भरी आवाज़ें फिर सुनाई नहीं देंगी। चक्की पर अनाज पीसने की आवाज़ कोई नहीं सुनेगा। उनके घरों में कोई दीपक जलता दिखाई नहीं देगा।

ru.L: И уничтожу у них звук радости и звук веселья, голос жениха и голос невесты, звук жерновов и свет светильника.
ru.B: Я прекращу у них звуки радости и веселья, голоса жениха и невесты, шум жерновов и свет светильника.
ru.R: Я положу конец звукам радости и счастья среди них. Никто не услышит весёлых голосов жениха и невесты на свадьбе. Никто не услышит, как мелют зерно на жерновах. Никто не увидит света лампы в их домах.

ja.L: わたしは彼らの中から、喜びの声と楽しみの声、花婿の声と花嫁の声、ひき臼の音と、ともしびの光を絶えさせる。
ja.B: わたしは彼らの中から、喜びの声と楽しみの声、花婿の声と花嫁の声、ひき臼の音と、ともしびの光を絶やす。
ja.R: わたしは、彼らの間から喜びと楽しみの声を消し去る。結婚式で花嫁と花婿が喜ぶ声も、もう聞こえなくなる。粉をひく臼の音も聞こえなくなり、家々にともしびの光も見えなくなる。

uk.L: І {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} зроблю, що зникне в них голос радості і голос веселощів, голос молодого і голос молодої, звук жорен і світло світильника.
uk.B: Я заберу в них звуки радості й веселощів, голоси молодого й молодої, гуркіт жорен і світло світильника.
uk.R: Я покладу край звукам радості й веселощів серед них. Ніхто не почує щасливих голосів молодої і молодого на їхньому весіллі. Ніхто не почує, як мелють зерно на жорнах. Ніхто не побачить світла світильника в їхніх домах.

decisions.choice: the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride: the joy of weddings, the sound of ordinary happy life
decisions.reason: As in 7:34 and 16:9. This verse adds two more signs of daily life to the list.

decisions.choice: the sound of the millstones and the light of the lamp: daily bread and a lived-in home
decisions.reason: Every household ground its grain each morning with a pair of hand millstones, and a small oil lamp burned in the house at night. When both stop, no one is left to bake bread or keep a home. Revelation 18:22-23 takes up the same pictures for the fall of Babylon.

decisions.choice: I will make perish: I will put an end to these sounds completely
decisions.reason: The verb means to destroy or make vanish. 7:34 says "I will make cease" with another verb; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the wording of 7:34 for joy, gladness, bridegroom and bride
decisions.reason: The same list keeps the same words at each level as in 7:34. Readable explains the millstones (grain being ground) and says that the lamps are in their homes.

decisions.choice: the wording of 7:34 for joy, gladness, bridegroom and bride
decisions.reason: The same Vietnamese words as the drafted 7:34 at each level, as the English keeps that verse's wording; 33:11 reverses them in the same words.

decisions.choice: हर्ष का शब्द और आनंद का शब्द, दूल्हे का शब्द और दुल्हन का शब्द (L); स्वर (B); आवाज़ें (R)
decisions.reason: The list keeps the wording of Jeremiah 16:9 in this translation at each level, as the English keeps 7:34 and 16:9.

decisions.choice: звук радости и звук веселья, голос жениха и голос невесты (L)
decisions.reason: The list keeps the wording of 7:34 and 16:9 at each level, as the English does.

decisions.choice: The wedding line in the words of JER.7.34 and 16:9 ("喜びの声と楽しみの声、花婿の声と花嫁の声" L, B; R "結婚式で花嫁と花婿が喜ぶ声"); qol recheim "ひき臼の音", 'or ner "ともしびの光".
decisions.reason: JER conventions: one wording for the repeated line.

source.text: וְהָֽיְתָה֙ כָּל־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את לְחָרְבָּ֖ה לְשַׁמָּ֑ה וְעָ֨בְד֜וּ הַגּוֹיִ֥ם הָאֵ֛לֶּה אֶת־מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל שִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will become all the land this a ruin, a horror, and will serve the nations these [the] king of Babylon seventy year[s].

en.L: And this whole land will become a ruin [and] a horror, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon seventy years.
en.B: This whole land will become a desolate ruin, and for seventy years these nations will serve the king of Babylon.
en.R: This whole land will become an empty ruin, a terrible sight. These nations will serve the king of Babylon for seventy years.

es.L: Y toda esta tierra será una ruina [y] un horror, y estas naciones servirán al rey de Babilonia setenta años.
es.B: Toda esta tierra quedará convertida en una ruina desolada, y durante setenta años estas naciones servirán al rey de Babilonia.
es.R: Toda esta tierra se convertirá en una ruina vacía, algo horrible de ver. Estas naciones servirán al rey de Babilonia durante setenta años.

fr.L: Et tout ce pays deviendra une ruine [et] une horreur, et ces nations serviront le roi de Babylone soixante-dix ans.
fr.B: Tout ce pays deviendra une ruine désolée, et pendant soixante-dix ans ces nations serviront le roi de Babylone.
fr.R: Tout ce pays deviendra une ruine vide, un spectacle terrible. Ces nations seront au service du roi de Babylone pendant soixante-dix ans.

sw.L: Na nchi hii yote itakuwa magofu [na] kitisho, na mataifa haya yatamtumikia mfalme wa Babeli miaka sabini.
sw.B: Nchi hii yote itakuwa magofu matupu, na kwa miaka sabini mataifa haya yatamtumikia mfalme wa Babeli.
sw.R: Nchi hii yote itakuwa magofu matupu, mahali pa kutisha. Mataifa haya yatamtumikia mfalme wa Babeli kwa miaka sabini.

vi.L: Cả xứ này sẽ thành nơi hoang tàn [và] một điều kinh hoàng, và các dân tộc này sẽ phục dịch vua Ba-by-lôn bảy mươi năm.
vi.B: Cả xứ này sẽ thành một nơi hoang tàn đổ nát, và các dân tộc này sẽ phục dịch vua Ba-by-lôn trong bảy mươi năm.
vi.R: Cả xứ này sẽ thành một nơi đổ nát trống không, một cảnh tượng khủng khiếp. Các dân tộc này sẽ phục dịch vua Ba-by-lôn trong bảy mươi năm.

ko.L: 그리고 이 온 땅이 폐허와 공포가 될 것이고, 이 민족들은 70년 동안 바빌론 왕을 섬길 것이다.
ko.B: 이 온 땅은 황폐한 폐허가 될 것이고, 이 민족들은 70년 동안 바빌론 왕을 섬길 것이다.
ko.R: 이 온 땅은 텅 빈 폐허, 끔찍한 곳이 될 것이다. 이 민족들은 70년 동안 바빌론 왕을 섬길 것이다.

pt.L: E toda esta terra se tornará uma ruína [e] um horror, e estas nações servirão o rei da Babilônia setenta anos.
pt.B: Toda esta terra se tornará uma ruína desolada, e durante setenta anos estas nações servirão o rei da Babilônia.
pt.R: Toda esta terra vai virar uma ruína vazia, uma visão terrível. Estas nações vão servir o rei da Babilônia durante setenta anos.

am.L: ይህችም ምድር ሁሉ ፍርስራሽና ድንጋጤ ትሆናለች፤ እነዚህም ሕዝቦች የባቢሎንን ንጉሥ ሰባ ዓመት ያገለግላሉ።
am.B: ይህች ምድር ሁሉ ባድማና ፍርስራሽ ትሆናለች፤ እነዚህም ሕዝቦች ለሰባ ዓመት የባቢሎንን ንጉሥ ያገለግላሉ።
am.R: ይህች ምድር ሁሉ ባዶ ፍርስራሽ፣ የሚያስደነግጥ ትዕይንት ትሆናለች። እነዚህ ሕዝቦች ለሰባ ዓመት የባቢሎንን ንጉሥ ያገለግላሉ።

hi.L: और यह सारा देश खंडहर [और] भय का कारण बन जाएगा, और ये जातियाँ सत्तर वर्ष तक बाबुल के राजा की सेवा करेंगी।
hi.B: यह सारा देश उजाड़ खंडहर बन जाएगा, और ये देश सत्तर वर्ष तक बाबुल के राजा की सेवा करेंगे।
hi.R: यह सारा देश सूना खंडहर बन जाएगा, एक भयानक दृश्य। ये देश सत्तर वर्ष तक बाबुल के राजा की सेवा करेंगे।

ru.L: И станет вся эта земля развалинами [и] ужасом, и эти народы будут служить царю Вавилона семьдесят лет.
ru.B: Вся эта земля станет опустошёнными развалинами, и семьдесят лет эти народы будут служить царю Вавилона.
ru.R: Вся эта земля станет пустыми развалинами, страшным местом. Эти народы будут служить царю Вавилона семьдесят лет.

ja.L: この地全体は廃墟となり、恐怖となる。これらの国々は七十年の間、バビロンの王に仕える。
ja.B: この地全体は荒れ果てた廃墟となり、これらの国々は七十年の間、バビロンの王に仕える。
ja.R: この国全体は、だれもいない廃墟となり、恐ろしい有様になる。これらの国々は、七十年の間、バビロンの王に仕える。

uk.L: І вся ця земля стане руїною, жахом, і ці народи служитимуть цареві Вавилону сімдесят років.
uk.B: Уся ця земля стане спустошеною руїною, і сімдесят років ці народи служитимуть цареві Вавилону.
uk.R: Уся ця земля стане порожньою руїною, страшним видовищем. Ці народи служитимуть цареві Вавилону сімдесят років.

decisions.choice: seventy years: the full span set for Babylon's rule, after which God will act
alternatives: an exact count of seventy years
a round number for a lifetime
decisions.reason: Seventy years is a full lifetime (Psalm 90:10) and a round number for a complete period (Isaiah 23:15 says the same of Tyre). Babylon's rule over the region lasted from about 605 BC, the year of this message, until Babylon fell to Cyrus in 539 BC, close to seventy years. Others count from the temple's destruction in 586 BC to its rebuilding in 516 BC, exactly seventy. The number returns in 29:10, where it marks the time before the exiles return. 2 Chronicles 36:21 reads it as the land keeping its missed sabbaths (Leviticus 26:34-35), Zechariah 1:12 and 7:5 count it in their own day, and Daniel 9:2 tells of Daniel reading this prophecy and praying, with an answer that speaks of seventy weeks (Daniel 9:24). The text gives a set time; how its years were counted is not stated.

decisions.choice: a ruin, a horror: a desolate land that appalls those who see it
decisions.reason: The second word is the one translated "horror" in verse 9. Of a land it describes both the desolation and the shock of those who see it.

decisions.choice: these nations: Judah and the neighboring nations named in verse 9
decisions.reason: "These nations" points back to the nations around Judah in verse 9; Judah is included with them under Babylon.

decisions.choice: a desolate ruin (B); an empty ruin, a terrible sight (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced joins the two nouns into one phrase; Readable keeps both ideas, the emptiness and the shock.

decisions.choice: setenta años
decisions.reason: The seventy years keep the published wording of 2 Chronicles 36:21 at every level.

decisions.choice: miaka sabini
decisions.reason: As 2 Chronicles 36:21, so the reader can see the number that Chronicles and Daniel take up.

decisions.choice: "soixante-dix ans"
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets: the French of France, never "septante", for the seventy years throughout.

decisions.choice: "bảy mươi năm"
decisions.reason: The seventy years, worded as in 2 Chronicles 36:21 (terms note), the same here and in 29:10.

decisions.choice: "70년", in figures at every level
decisions.reason: The terms note writes the seventy years in figures at every level, as 2 Chronicles 36:21.

decisions.choice: setenta anos (every level)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also verse 12 and 29:10), as the shared rules for Jeremiah ask: the span set for Babylon's rule (m1) is "setenta anos" at every level, the number in words as Portuguese writes round tens, so the two prophecies read alike.

decisions.choice: सत्तर वर्ष
decisions.reason: The seventy years are सत्तर वर्ष at every level, the wording of 2 Chronicles 36:21 and Daniel 9:2, which cite this prophecy; the same at 25:12 and 29:10.

decisions.choice: семьдесят лет
decisions.reason: The seventy years keep the plain number, as 2 Chronicles 36:21 and Daniel 9:2 have it in this translation, so a reader can follow the promise from Jeremiah to them.

source.text: וְהָיָ֣ה כִמְלֹ֣אות שִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֡ה אֶפְקֹ֣ד עַל־מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶל֩ וְעַל־הַגּ֨וֹי הַה֧וּא נְאֻם־יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־עֲוֺנָ֖ם וְעַל־אֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים וְשַׂמְתִּ֥י אֹת֖וֹ לְשִֽׁמְמ֥וֹת עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, when are completed seventy year[s], I will visit on [the] king of Babylon and on the nation that, declaration of Yahweh, their iniquity, and on [the] land of [the] Chaldeans, and I will make it desolations of forever.

en.L: And it will be, when seventy years are completed, I will punish the king of Babylon and that nation, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for their iniquity, and the land of the Chaldeans, and I will make it an everlasting desolation.
en.B: But when the seventy years are over, I will punish the king of Babylon and that nation for their guilt, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will punish the land of the Chaldeans and make it a desolation forever.
en.R: But when the seventy years are over, I will punish the king of Babylon and his nation for their sins, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will punish the land of the Babylonians and make it an empty waste forever.

es.L: Y sucederá que cuando se hayan cumplido los setenta años, castigaré al rey de Babilonia y a aquella nación, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, por su iniquidad, y a la tierra de los caldeos, y la convertiré en desolación eterna.
es.B: Pero cuando se cumplan los setenta años, castigaré al rey de Babilonia y a aquella nación por su culpa, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Castigaré la tierra de los caldeos y la convertiré en una desolación para siempre.
es.R: Pero cuando se cumplan los setenta años, castigaré al rey de Babilonia y a su nación por sus pecados, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Castigaré la tierra de los babilonios y la convertiré en un desierto para siempre.

fr.L: Et il arrivera, quand les soixante-dix ans seront accomplis, que je punirai le roi de Babylone et cette nation, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, pour leur iniquité, ainsi que le pays des Chaldéens, et j’en ferai une désolation éternelle.
fr.B: Mais quand les soixante-dix ans seront passés, je punirai le roi de Babylone et cette nation pour leur faute, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Je punirai le pays des Chaldéens et j’en ferai une désolation pour toujours.
fr.R: Mais quand les soixante-dix ans seront passés, je punirai le roi de Babylone et son peuple pour leurs péchés, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Je punirai le pays des Babyloniens et j’en ferai un désert vide pour toujours.

sw.L: Na itakuwa, miaka sabini itakapotimia, nitamwadhibu mfalme wa Babeli na taifa lile, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa uovu wao, na nchi ya Wakaldayo, nami nitaifanya kuwa ukiwa wa milele.
sw.B: Lakini miaka sabini itakapokwisha, nitamwadhibu mfalme wa Babeli na taifa lile kwa hatia yao, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Nitaiadhibu nchi ya Wakaldayo na kuifanya kuwa ukiwa milele.
sw.R: Lakini miaka sabini itakapokwisha, nitamwadhibu mfalme wa Babeli na taifa lake kwa dhambi zao, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Nitaiadhibu nchi ya Wababeli na kuifanya kuwa nyika tupu milele.

vi.L: Khi bảy mươi năm đã mãn, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ phạt vua Ba-by-lôn và dân tộc ấy, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, vì tội ác của chúng, cùng xứ của người Canh-đê, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho nó thành nơi hoang vu đời đời.
vi.B: Nhưng khi bảy mươi năm đã mãn, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ phạt vua Ba-by-lôn và dân tộc ấy vì tội lỗi của chúng, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy. Ta sẽ phạt xứ của người Canh-đê và làm cho nó thành nơi hoang vu mãi mãi.
vi.R: Nhưng khi bảy mươi năm đã qua, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ phạt vua Ba-by-lôn và dân tộc của vua ấy vì tội lỗi của chúng, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán. Ta sẽ phạt xứ của người Ba-by-lôn và làm cho nó thành một nơi hoang vắng mãi mãi.

ko.L: 그리고 70년이 차면, 내가 바빌론 왕과 그 민족을 그들의 죄악 때문에 벌하고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다, 갈대아 사람들의 땅도 벌하여 그 땅을 영원한 황무지로 만들겠다.
ko.B: 그러나 70년이 다 차면, 내가 바빌론 왕과 그 민족을 그들의 죄 때문에 벌하겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 내가 갈대아 사람들의 땅을 벌하여 영원히 황무지로 만들겠다.
ko.R: 그러나 70년이 끝나면, 내가 바빌론 왕과 그의 나라를 그들이 지은 죄 때문에 벌하겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 내가 바빌로니아 사람들의 땅을 벌하여 영원히 텅 빈 땅으로 만들겠다.

pt.L: E acontecerá que, quando se completarem setenta anos, farei o rei da Babilônia e aquela nação prestarem contas, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, da sua iniquidade, e também a terra dos caldeus, e farei dela uma desolação eterna.
pt.B: Mas, quando se completarem os setenta anos, castigarei o rei da Babilônia e aquela nação pela sua culpa, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}. Castigarei a terra dos caldeus e farei dela uma desolação para sempre.
pt.R: Mas, quando os setenta anos terminarem, vou castigar o rei da Babilônia e o seu povo pelos seus pecados, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}. Vou castigar a terra dos babilônios e transformá-la num deserto vazio para sempre.

am.L: እንዲህም ይሆናል፤ ሰባው ዓመት በተፈጸመ ጊዜ የባቢሎንን ንጉሥና ያን ሕዝብ፣ ይላል {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}፣ ስለ በደላቸው እቀጣለሁ፤ የከለዳውያንንም ምድር [እቀጣለሁ]፤ ለዘላለምም ባድማ አደርጋታለሁ።
am.B: ሰባው ዓመት ሲፈጸም ግን የባቢሎንን ንጉሥና ያን ሕዝብ ስለ በደላቸው እቀጣለሁ፣ ይላል {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}። የከለዳውያንን ምድር እቀጣለሁ፤ ለዘላለምም ባድማ አደርጋታለሁ።
am.R: ሰባው ዓመት ሲፈጸም ግን የባቢሎንን ንጉሥና ሕዝቡን ስለ ኃጢአታቸው እቀጣለሁ፣ ይላል {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}። የባቢሎናውያንን ምድር እቀጣለሁ፤ ለዘላለምም ባዶ ምድረ በዳ አደርጋታለሁ።

hi.L: और ऐसा होगा कि जब सत्तर वर्ष पूरे हो जाएँगे, तब मैं बाबुल के राजा को और उस जाति को उनके अधर्म का दंड दूँगा, {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} की यह वाणी है, और कसदियों के देश को भी, और मैं उसे सदा के लिए उजाड़ बना दूँगा।
hi.B: पर जब सत्तर वर्ष पूरे हो जाएँगे, तब मैं बाबुल के राजा को और उस देश को उनके दोष का दंड दूँगा, {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} की यह वाणी है। मैं कसदियों के देश को दंड दूँगा और उसे सदा के लिए उजाड़ बना दूँगा।
hi.R: पर जब सत्तर वर्ष पूरे हो जाएँगे, तब मैं बाबुल के राजा को और उसकी प्रजा को उनके पापों का दंड दूँगा, {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} कहते हैं। मैं बाबुलियों के देश को दंड दूँगा और उसे सदा के लिए सूना बना दूँगा।

ru.L: И будет, когда исполнятся семьдесят лет, {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} накажу царя Вавилона и тот народ, — слово {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}, — за их беззаконие, и землю халдеев, и сделаю её вечным опустошением.
ru.B: Но когда исполнятся семьдесят лет, {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} накажу царя Вавилона и тот народ за их вину, говорит {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}. Я накажу землю халдеев и сделаю её пустыней навеки.
ru.R: Но когда пройдут семьдесят лет, {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} накажу царя Вавилона и его народ за их грехи, говорит {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}. Я накажу землю вавилонян и навсегда сделаю её пустой и заброшенной.

ja.L: 七十年が満ちるとき、わたしはバビロンの王とその国を、彼らの咎のゆえに罰する――{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の言葉――。またカルデア人の地を[罰し]、そこをとこしえの荒れ地とする。
ja.B: しかし、七十年が終わると、わたしはバビロンの王とその国を、その咎のゆえに罰する、と{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}は告げる。わたしはカルデア人の地を罰し、そこをいつまでも荒れ果てた地とする。
ja.R: しかし、七十年が終わると、わたしはバビロンの王とその国を、その罪のために罰する、と{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}は言う。わたしはバビロンの国を罰し、そこをいつまでも何もない荒れ地にする。

uk.L: І станеться, коли сповняться сімдесят років, {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} покараю царя Вавилону і той народ, говорить {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}, за їхню провину, і край халдеїв, і зроблю його вічним спустошенням.
uk.B: Але коли сімдесят років скінчаться, {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} покараю царя Вавилону і той народ за їхню провину, говорить {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}. Я покараю край халдеїв і зроблю його спустошеним навіки.
uk.R: Але коли сімдесят років скінчаться, {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} покараю царя Вавилону і його народ за їхні гріхи, каже {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}. Я покараю край вавилонян і зроблю його порожньою пусткою навіки.

decisions.choice: I will visit on ... their iniquity: I will punish them for their guilt
decisions.reason: To "visit" a sin on someone is to bring its punishment on them (5:9; Exodus 20:5). Babylon was God's instrument, but it would answer for its own cruelty and pride (50:29-32; 51:24).

decisions.choice: when seventy years are completed: the limit God has set to Babylon's rule
decisions.reason: See verse 11. The judgment on Judah has an end, and the nation that brought it will be judged in turn; chapters 50-51 spell this out.

decisions.choice: the land of the Chaldeans: Babylonia
decisions.reason: The Chaldeans were the people of southern Mesopotamia whose kings ruled Babylon in Jeremiah's time, so the name stands for the Babylonians.

decisions.choice: iniquity (L), guilt (B), sins (R); Chaldeans (L, B), Babylonians (R)
decisions.reason: The set wording for these terms, as in Isaiah. Balanced and Readable repeat "I will punish" before the land to make the sentence clear.

decisions.choice: अधर्म (L); दोष (B); पाप (R)
decisions.reason: ʿavon is अधर्म at Literal and दोष at Balanced, as the Pentateuch note sets it; Readable says पाप, as the English Readable says "sins".

decisions.choice: беззаконие (L), вина (B), грехи (R); халдеи (L, B), вавилоняне (R)
decisions.reason: Iniquity takes the Pentateuch note's words (беззаконие, вина), Readable "грехи" as the English; the Kasdim are "халдеи" at Literal and Balanced and "вавилоняне" at Readable, as in 24:5.

decisions.choice: 'efqod … 'et 'avonam "彼らの咎のゆえに罰する" (L, B), "その罪のために罰する" (R); 'erets Kasdim "カルデア人の地" (L, B), "バビロンの国" (R).
decisions.reason: m1; 'avon 咎 (L, B), 罪 (R) as the prophetic convention.

source.text: וְהֵֽבֵאתִי֙ עַל־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַהִ֔יא אֶת־כָּל־דְּבָרַ֖י אֲשֶׁר־דִּבַּ֣רְתִּי עָלֶ֑יהָ אֵ֤ת כָּל־הַכָּתוּב֙ בַּסֵּ֣פֶר הַזֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־נִבָּ֥א יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ עַל־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will bring on the land that all my words which I have spoken against it, all the [thing] written in the book this, which prophesied Jeremiah against all the nations.

en.L: And I will bring on that land all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words that I have spoken against it, all that is written in this book, which Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.
en.B: I will bring on that land everything I have said against it, all that is written in this book, which Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.
en.R: I will make everything I have said against Babylon come true. All of it is written in this book. It is what Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.

es.L: Y traeré sobre esa tierra todas {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras que he hablado contra ella, todo lo que está escrito en este libro, lo que profetizó Jeremías contra todas las naciones.
es.B: Traeré sobre esa tierra todo lo que he dicho contra ella, todo lo que está escrito en este libro, lo que Jeremías profetizó contra todas las naciones.
es.R: Haré que se cumpla todo lo que he dicho contra Babilonia. Todo está escrito en este libro. Es lo que Jeremías profetizó contra todas las naciones.

fr.L: Et je ferai venir sur ce pays toutes {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles que j’ai prononcées contre lui, tout ce qui est écrit dans ce livre, ce que Jérémie a prophétisé contre toutes les nations.
fr.B: Je ferai venir sur ce pays tout ce que j’ai annoncé contre lui, tout ce qui est écrit dans ce livre, ce que Jérémie a prophétisé contre toutes les nations.
fr.R: Je ferai arriver tout ce que j’ai annoncé contre Babylone. Tout cela est écrit dans ce livre. C’est ce que Jérémie a prophétisé contre toutes les nations.

sw.L: Nami nitaleta juu ya nchi ile maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} yote niliyoyanena juu yake, yote yaliyoandikwa katika kitabu hiki, ambayo Yeremia alitabiri juu ya mataifa yote.
sw.B: Nitaleta juu ya nchi ile kila kitu nilichosema dhidi yake, yote yaliyoandikwa katika kitabu hiki, ambayo Yeremia alitabiri dhidi ya mataifa yote.
sw.R: Nitafanya yatimie yote niliyosema dhidi ya Babeli. Yote yameandikwa katika kitabu hiki. Ndiyo yale ambayo Yeremia alitabiri dhidi ya mataifa yote.

vi.L: Ta sẽ giáng trên xứ ấy mọi lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã phán nghịch cùng nó, mọi điều đã chép trong sách này, là điều Giê-rê-mi đã nói tiên tri nghịch cùng mọi dân tộc.
vi.B: Ta sẽ giáng trên xứ ấy mọi điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã phán nghịch cùng nó, mọi điều đã chép trong sách này, là điều Giê-rê-mi đã nói tiên tri nghịch cùng mọi dân tộc.
vi.R: Ta sẽ làm cho mọi điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã phán nghịch cùng Ba-by-lôn đều xảy ra. Tất cả đều được chép trong sách này. Đó là điều Giê-rê-mi đã nói tiên tri nghịch cùng mọi dân tộc.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 그 땅에 대하여 말한 내 모든 말, 곧 예레미야가 모든 민족에 대하여 예언하여 이 책에 기록된 모든 것을 그 땅에 이루겠다.
ko.B: 내가 그 땅에 대하여 말한 모든 것, 곧 예레미야가 모든 민족에 대하여 예언한 것으로서 이 책에 기록된 모든 것을 그 땅에 이루겠다.
ko.R: 내가 바빌론에 대하여 한 모든 말이 그대로 이루어지게 하겠다. 그 말은 모두 이 책에 기록되어 있다. 그것은 예레미야가 모든 민족에 대하여 예언한 것이다.

pt.L: E trarei sobre aquela terra todas as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} palavras que falei contra ela, tudo o que está escrito neste livro, que Jeremias profetizou contra todas as nações.
pt.B: Trarei sobre aquela terra tudo o que eu disse contra ela, tudo o que está escrito neste livro, que Jeremias profetizou contra todas as nações.
pt.R: Vou fazer acontecer tudo o que eu disse contra a Babilônia. Tudo isso está escrito neste livro. É o que Jeremias profetizou contra todas as nações.

am.L: በዚያችም ምድር ላይ የተናገርኩባትን ቃሌን ሁሉ፣ ኤርምያስ በሕዝቦች ሁሉ ላይ ትንቢት የተናገረውን፣ በዚህ መጽሐፍ የተጻፈውን ሁሉ አመጣባታለሁ።
am.B: በዚያች ምድር ላይ የተናገርኩትን ሁሉ፣ ኤርምያስ በሕዝቦች ሁሉ ላይ ትንቢት የተናገረውን፣ በዚህ መጽሐፍ የተጻፈውን ሁሉ አመጣባታለሁ።
am.R: በባቢሎን ላይ የተናገርኩት ሁሉ እንዲፈጸም አደርጋለሁ። ይህ ሁሉ በዚህ መጽሐፍ ተጽፏል። ኤርምያስ በሕዝቦች ሁሉ ላይ የተናገረው ትንቢት ይህ ነው።

hi.L: और मैं उस देश पर अपने वे सब वचन ले आऊँगा जो मैंने उसके विरुद्ध कहे हैं, वह सब जो इस पुस्तक में लिखा है, जो यिर्मयाह ने सब जातियों के विरुद्ध भविष्यवाणी करके कहा है।
hi.B: मैं उस देश पर वह सब ले आऊँगा जो मैंने उसके विरुद्ध कहा है, वह सब जो इस पुस्तक में लिखा है, जिसकी भविष्यवाणी यिर्मयाह ने सब देशों के विरुद्ध की है।
hi.R: मैंने बाबुल के विरुद्ध जो कुछ कहा है, वह सब मैं पूरा करूँगा। वह सब इस पुस्तक में लिखा है। यह वही है जिसकी भविष्यवाणी यिर्मयाह ने सब देशों के विरुद्ध की है।

ru.L: И наведу на ту землю все {{deity_pronoun:мои|Мои}} слова, которые {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} изрёк против неё, всё написанное в этой книге, что пророчествовал Иеремия против всех народов.
ru.B: Я наведу на ту землю всё, что {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} сказал против неё, всё, что написано в этой книге, что Иеремия пророчествовал против всех народов.
ru.R: Я исполню всё, что {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} сказал против Вавилона. Всё это записано в этой книге. Это то, что Иеремия пророчествовал против всех народов.

ja.L: わたしは、その地について語ったわたしのすべての言葉、すなわち、エレミヤがすべての国々について預言した、この書に記されているすべてのことを、その地にもたらす。
ja.B: わたしは、その地について語ったすべてのことを、その地にもたらす。それは、エレミヤがすべての国々について預言した、この書に記されているすべてのことである。
ja.R: わたしは、バビロンに対して語ったすべてのことを、実際に起こす。そのすべては、この書に書かれている。それは、エレミヤがすべての国々について預言したことだ。

uk.L: І {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} наведу на той край усі {{deity_pronoun:мої|Мої}} слова, які {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} говорив проти нього, усе, що написано в цій книзі, що Єремія пророкував проти всіх народів.
uk.B: Я наведу на той край усе, що {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} сказав проти нього, усе, що написано в цій книзі, що Єремія пророкував проти всіх народів.
uk.R: Я зроблю так, що збудеться все, що {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} сказав проти Вавилону. Усе це написано в цій книзі. Це те, що Єремія пророкував проти всіх народів.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew order, in which the oracles against the nations come later in the book (chapters 46-51)
alternatives: the Greek order, with the oracles against the nations following here
decisions.reason: This is the point at which the Greek translation of Jeremiah places its oracles against the nations, which the Hebrew gives as chapters 46-51. In the Greek, the words "which Jeremiah prophesied against the nations" serve as the heading of those oracles, and the Greek lacks verse 14. See the note at 1:1. This translation follows the Hebrew order. These statements come from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: which Jeremiah prophesied: words that speak of Jeremiah in the third person, inside God's speech
decisions.reason: God has been speaking in the first person ("my words"), and here Jeremiah is named as the one who prophesied. The clause reads like a note that describes the book, joined to God's words; it shows that the prophet's messages were already being gathered in writing (compare 36:2, 32, dated to the same year).

decisions.choice: that land: Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans in verse 12
decisions.reason: "That land" and "against it" refer to the land of the Chaldeans just named.

decisions.choice: Babylon
decisions.reason: Readable names the land so that no reader takes "that land" to be Judah.

decisions.choice: "예레미야가" named in the third person inside God's speech
decisions.reason: As the Hebrew (meaning decision m2), God's words speak of Jeremiah by name; Korean keeps it rather than turning it into "you".

source.text: כִּ֣י עָֽבְדוּ־בָ֤ם גַּם־הֵ֨מָּה֙ גּוֹיִ֣ם רַבִּ֔ים וּמְלָכִ֖ים גְּדוֹלִ֑ים וְשִׁלַּמְתִּ֥י לָהֶ֛ם כְּפָעֳלָ֖ם וּכְמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיהֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For will make serve them also they nations many and kings great, and I will repay them according to their deed[s] and according to [the] work of their hands.

en.L: For many nations and great kings will make slaves of them also, and I will repay them according to their deeds and according to the work of their hands."
en.B: For many nations and great kings will make them serve in their turn, and I will repay them for what they have done, for the work of their hands."
en.R: Many nations and great kings will force the Babylonians to serve them, as they forced others to serve. I will pay them back for all the evil things they have done."

es.L: Porque también a ellos los harán esclavos muchas naciones y grandes reyes, y les pagaré conforme a sus hechos y conforme a la obra de sus manos».
es.B: Porque muchas naciones y grandes reyes los harán servir a su vez, y les pagaré por lo que han hecho, por la obra de sus manos».
es.R: Muchas naciones y grandes reyes obligarán a los babilonios a servirles, así como ellos obligaron a otros a servir. Les daré su merecido por todo el mal que han hecho».

fr.L: Car des nations nombreuses et de grands rois les asserviront eux aussi, et je leur rendrai selon leurs actions et selon l’œuvre de leurs mains. »
fr.B: Car des nations nombreuses et de grands rois les mettront à leur tour à leur service, et je leur rendrai ce qu’ils ont fait, l’œuvre de leurs mains. »
fr.R: Beaucoup de nations et de grands rois obligeront les Babyloniens à les servir, comme eux-mêmes ont obligé les autres à les servir. Je leur ferai payer tout le mal qu’ils ont fait. »

sw.L: Kwa maana mataifa mengi na wafalme wakuu watawatumikisha wao pia, nami nitawalipa sawasawa na matendo yao na sawasawa na kazi ya mikono yao."
sw.B: Kwa maana mataifa mengi na wafalme wakuu watawafanya nao watumike, nami nitawalipa kwa yale waliyoyatenda, kwa kazi ya mikono yao."
sw.R: Mataifa mengi na wafalme wakuu watawalazimisha Wababeli kuwatumikia, kama wao walivyowalazimisha wengine. Nitawalipa kwa maovu yote waliyoyatenda."

vi.L: Vì nhiều dân tộc và các vua lớn cũng sẽ bắt chúng làm nô lệ, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ báo trả chúng theo việc làm của chúng và theo công việc tay chúng."
vi.B: Vì đến lượt chúng, nhiều dân tộc và các vua lớn sẽ bắt chúng phục dịch, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ báo trả chúng theo những gì chúng đã làm, theo công việc tay chúng."
vi.R: Nhiều dân tộc và các vua lớn sẽ bắt người Ba-by-lôn phục dịch mình, như người Ba-by-lôn đã bắt người khác phục dịch. Ta sẽ báo trả chúng về mọi điều ác chúng đã làm."

ko.L: 많은 민족과 큰 왕들이 그들도 종으로 부릴 것이다. 내가 그들의 행위와 그들 손으로 한 일대로 그들에게 갚아 주겠다."
ko.B: 이제는 많은 민족과 큰 왕들이 그들을 종으로 부릴 것이다. 내가 그들이 한 일, 그들 손으로 저지른 일대로 그들에게 갚아 주겠다."
ko.R: 많은 민족과 큰 왕들이 바빌로니아 사람들을 종으로 부릴 것이다. 그들이 다른 민족들을 종으로 부렸던 것과 같다. 내가 그들이 저지른 모든 악한 일을 그대로 갚아 주겠다."

pt.L: Pois também a eles muitas nações e grandes reis farão escravos, e eu lhes retribuirei segundo as suas ações e segundo a obra das suas mãos."
pt.B: Pois muitas nações e grandes reis também os farão servir, e eu lhes retribuirei pelo que fizeram, pela obra das suas mãos."
pt.R: Muitas nações e grandes reis vão obrigar os babilônios a servi-los, assim como eles obrigaram outros a servir. Vou pagar a eles de volta por todas as coisas más que fizeram."

am.L: ብዙ ሕዝቦችና ታላላቅ ነገሥታት እነርሱንም ደግሞ ባሪያዎች ያደርጓቸዋልና፤ እኔም እንደ ሥራቸውና እንደ እጃቸው ሥራ እከፍላቸዋለሁ።»
am.B: ብዙ ሕዝቦችና ታላላቅ ነገሥታት በተራቸው እነርሱን ያስገዟቸዋልና፤ እኔም እንደ ሥራቸውና እንደ እጃቸው ሥራ እመልስባቸዋለሁ።»
am.R: ባቢሎናውያን ሌሎችን እንዳስገዙ፣ ብዙ ሕዝቦችና ታላላቅ ነገሥታት እነርሱን ያስገዟቸዋል። ስለ ሠሩት ክፉ ነገር ሁሉ የሚገባቸውን እከፍላቸዋለሁ።»

hi.L: क्योंकि बहुत सी जातियाँ और बड़े बड़े राजा उन्हें भी अपना दास बनाएँगे, और मैं उन्हें उनके कामों के अनुसार और उनके हाथों के काम के अनुसार बदला दूँगा।"
hi.B: क्योंकि बहुत से देश और बड़े बड़े राजा उनसे भी अपनी सेवा करवाएँगे, और मैं उन्हें उनके कामों का, उनके हाथों के काम का बदला दूँगा।"
hi.R: बहुत से देश और बड़े बड़े राजा बाबुलियों से अपनी सेवा करवाएँगे, जैसे उन्होंने दूसरों से करवाई थी। मैं उन्हें उनके सब बुरे कामों का बदला दूँगा।"

ru.L: Ведь поработят их также многие народы и великие цари, и {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} воздам им по их делам и по делу их рук.»
ru.B: Ведь и их заставят служить многие народы и великие цари, и {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} воздам им за то, что они сделали, за дело их рук.»
ru.R: Многие народы и великие цари заставят вавилонян служить себе, как вавилоняне заставляли служить других. Я воздам им за всё зло, которое они сделали.»

ja.L: 実に、多くの国々と大いなる王たちが、彼らをも奴隷として仕えさせる。わたしは彼らの行いに応じ、彼らの手のわざに応じて、彼らに報いる。」
ja.B: 多くの国々と大いなる王たちが、今度は彼らを仕えさせる。わたしは彼らの行いに応じ、その手のわざに応じて、彼らに報いる。」
ja.R: 多くの国々と強い王たちが、今度はバビロン人を自分たちに仕えさせる。バビロン人がほかの国々を仕えさせたのと同じだ。わたしは、彼らがしたすべての悪いことに応じて、彼らに報いる。」

uk.L: Бо й їх поневолять багато народів і великі царі, і {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} відплачу їм за їхніми вчинками і за ділом їхніх рук».
uk.B: Бо багато народів і великих царів змусять і їх служити, і {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} відплачу їм за те, що вони зробили, за діло їхніх рук».
uk.R: Багато народів і великих царів змусять вавилонян служити їм, так само як вавилоняни змушували служити інших. Я відплачу їм за все зло, яке вони вчинили».

decisions.choice: will make slaves of them also: those who subjected the nations will in turn be subjected
decisions.reason: The same verb "serve" used in verse 11 of the nations serving Babylon now turns on Babylon itself. "Also they" stresses the reversal (27:7; 50:9; 51:27-28).

decisions.choice: according to their deeds and the work of their hands: in full measure for what they did
decisions.reason: The pair of phrases means all their conduct. "The work of their hands" here means their deeds, not idols as in verses 6-7 (50:29).

decisions.choice: make slaves of (L); make ... serve (B, R)
decisions.reason: The style guide gives "slave" at Literal and "make ... serve" at Balanced and Readable for the verb of enslaving. Readable names the Babylonians and supplies "as they forced others to serve" to show the reversal.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah's speech closes here
decisions.reason: The quotation that opened at verse 3 ends with this verse. Verse 15 begins a new account.

decisions.choice: "bắt ... làm nô lệ" (Literal); "bắt ... phục dịch" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the verb is real subjection of nations, not God's service, so Literal can say "nô lệ" as the English "make slaves of"; Balanced and Readable say "phục dịch", the word of verse 11.

decisions.choice: 'avdu vam gam hemmah "彼らをも奴隷として仕えさせる" (L), "今度は彼らを仕えさせる" (B), "今度はバビロン人を…仕えさせる" (R).
decisions.reason: m1: the subjugators subjected in turn; 奴隷 at L where the English L says "make slaves".

source.text: כִּ֣י כֹה֩ אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֵלַ֔י קַ֠ח אֶת־כּ֨וֹס הַיַּ֧יִן הַחֵמָ֛ה הַזֹּ֖את מִיָּדִ֑י וְהִשְׁקִיתָ֤ה אֹתוֹ֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָנֹכִ֛י שֹׁלֵ֥חַ אוֹתְךָ֖ אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For thus said Yahweh [the] God of Israel to me: Take the cup of the wine, the wrath, this from my hand, and make drink it all the nations that I [am] sending you to them.

en.L: For thus {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, said to me: "Take this cup of the wine of wrath from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand, and make all the nations to whom I am sending you drink it.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, said this to me: "Take this cup filled with the wine of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand, and make all the nations I am sending you to drink it.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, said to me, "Here is a cup in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand. It is filled with wine, and the wine is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger. Take it. Then go to all the nations I am sending you to, and make them drink it.

es.L: Porque así me dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel: «Toma de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano esta copa del vino de la ira, y haz que beban de ella todas las naciones a las que yo te envío.
es.B: Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, me dijo esto: «Toma de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano esta copa llena del vino de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira, y haz que la beban todas las naciones a las que te envío.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, me dijo: «Aquí hay una copa en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano. Está llena de vino, y el vino es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira. Tómala. Luego ve a todas las naciones a las que te envío y haz que la beban.

fr.L: Car ainsi me parla {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël : « Prends de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main cette coupe du vin de la fureur, et fais-la boire à toutes les nations vers lesquelles je t’envoie.
fr.B: Car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël, me dit ceci : « Prends de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main cette coupe remplie du vin de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} fureur, et fais-la boire à toutes les nations vers lesquelles je t’envoie.
fr.R: Voici ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël, m’a dit : « Voici une coupe dans {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main. Elle est remplie de vin, et ce vin, c’est {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère. Prends-la. Ensuite, va voir toutes les nations vers lesquelles je t’envoie, et fais-les boire.

sw.L: Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, aliniambia hivi: "Kikombe hiki cha divai ya ghadhabu ukichukue mkononi {{deity_pronoun:mwangu|Mwangu}}, uyanyweshe mataifa yote ninayokutuma kwao.
sw.B: Kwa maana hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, aliniambia: "Chukua mkononi {{deity_pronoun:mwangu|Mwangu}} kikombe hiki kilichojaa divai ya ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, uyanyweshe mataifa yote ninayokutuma kwao.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, aliniambia, "Tazama kikombe kilicho mkononi {{deity_pronoun:mwangu|Mwangu}}. Kimejaa divai, na divai hiyo ni hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Kichukue. Kisha nenda kwa mataifa yote ninayokutuma kwao, uwanyweshe.

vi.L: Vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, đã phán với tôi thế này: "Hãy lấy chén rượu thịnh nộ này khỏi tay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và cho mọi dân tộc mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sai ngươi đến uống chén ấy.
vi.B: Vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, đã phán với tôi như vầy: "Con hãy lấy khỏi tay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chén đầy rượu thịnh nộ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} này, và cho mọi dân tộc {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sai con đến uống chén ấy.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, đã phán với tôi: "Đây là một cái chén trong tay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Chén ấy đầy rượu, và rượu ấy là cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Con hãy lấy chén ấy. Rồi hãy đi đến mọi dân tộc {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sai con đến, và bắt họ uống chén ấy.

ko.L: 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 이와 같이 말씀하셨다. "진노의 포도주가 담긴 이 잔을 내 손에서 받아, 내가 너를 보내는 모든 민족에게 그것을 마시게 하여라.
ko.B: 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 이렇게 말씀하셨다. "내 진노의 포도주가 가득 담긴 이 잔을 내 손에서 받아, 내가 너를 보내는 모든 민족에게 마시게 하여라.
ko.R: 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. "내 손에 잔이 하나 있다. 그 잔에는 포도주가 가득 차 있는데, 그 포도주는 나의 진노다. 이 잔을 받아라. 그리고 내가 너를 보내는 모든 민족에게 가서 그들이 이 잔을 마시게 하여라.

pt.L: Pois assim me disse {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de Israel: "Toma da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mão este cálice do vinho do furor, e dá-o a beber a todas as nações às quais eu te envio.
pt.B: Pois assim me disse {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de Israel: "Toma da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mão este cálice cheio do vinho do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} furor e faze todas as nações às quais eu te envio bebê-lo.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de Israel, me disse: "Aqui está um cálice na {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mão. Ele está cheio de vinho, e o vinho é a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} ira. Toma esse cálice. Depois vai a todas as nações às quais eu te envio e faze-as beber.

am.L: የእስራኤል አምላክ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንዲህ ብሎኛልና፦ «ይህን የቁጣ ወይን ጽዋ ከእጄ ውሰድ፤ እኔ የምልክህ ሕዝቦችም ሁሉ እንዲጠጡት አድርግ።
am.B: የእስራኤል አምላክ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንዲህ ብሎኛልና፦ «በቁጣዬ ወይን የተሞላውን ይህን ጽዋ ከእጄ ውሰድ፤ የምልክህንም ሕዝቦች ሁሉ አጠጣቸው።
am.R: የእስራኤል አምላክ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንዲህ አለኝ፦ «በእጄ ጽዋ አለ። በወይን ጠጅ ተሞልቷል፤ የወይን ጠጁም ቁጣዬ ነው። ውሰደው። ከዚያም ወደምልክህ ሕዝቦች ሁሉ ሂድና እንዲጠጡት አድርግ።

hi.L: क्योंकि {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, इस्राएल के परमेश्वर, ने मुझसे यों कहा: "क्रोध की मदिरा का यह कटोरा मेरे हाथ से ले, और उन सब जातियों को, जिनके पास मैं तुम्हें भेज रहा हूँ, उसे पिलाओ।
hi.B: क्योंकि {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, इस्राएल के परमेश्वर, ने मुझसे यह कहा: "मेरे क्रोध की मदिरा से भरा यह कटोरा मेरे हाथ से लो, और उन सब देशों को जिनके पास मैं तुम्हें भेज रहा हूँ, उसे पिलाओ।
hi.R: {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, इस्राएल के परमेश्वर, ने मुझसे कहा, "मेरे हाथ में एक कटोरा है। वह मदिरा से भरा है, और वह मदिरा मेरा क्रोध है। इसे ले लो। फिर उन सब देशों के पास जाओ जिनके पास मैं तुम्हें भेज रहा हूँ, और उन्हें इसमें से पिलाओ।

ru.L: Ведь так сказал мне {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}, Бог Израиля: «Возьми эту чашу вина ярости из {{deity_pronoun:моей|Моей}} руки и напои ею все народы, к которым {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} посылаю тебя.
ru.B: Ведь так сказал мне {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}, Бог Израиля: «Возьми из {{deity_pronoun:моей|Моей}} руки эту чашу, полную вина {{deity_pronoun:моей|Моей}} ярости, и напои ею все народы, к которым {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} посылаю тебя.
ru.R: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}, Бог Израиля, сказал мне: «Вот чаша в {{deity_pronoun:моей|Моей}} руке. Она полна вина, и это вино — {{deity_pronoun:мой|Мой}} гнев. Возьми её. Потом иди ко всем народам, к которым {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} тебя посылаю, и заставь их выпить из неё.

ja.L: イスラエルの神、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}は、わたしにこう言われたからである。「この憤りのぶどう酒の杯を、わたしの手から取り、わたしがあなたを遣わすすべての国々に、それを飲ませなさい。
ja.B: イスラエルの神、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}は、わたしにこう言われた。「わたしの憤りのぶどう酒で満ちたこの杯を、わたしの手から受け取り、わたしがあなたを遣わすすべての国々に、それを飲ませなさい。
ja.R: イスラエルの神、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}は、わたしにこう言われました。「ここに、わたしの手にある杯がある。それはぶどう酒で満ちている。そのぶどう酒は、わたしの怒りだ。それを受け取りなさい。そして、わたしがあなたを遣わすすべての国々に行き、彼らにそれを飲ませなさい。

uk.L: Бо так сказав мені {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}, Бог Ізраїля: «Візьми цю чашу вина гніву з {{deity_pronoun:моєї|Моєї}} руки і напій нею всі народи, до яких {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} посилаю тебе.
uk.B: Бо {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}, Бог Ізраїля, сказав мені таке: «Візьми з {{deity_pronoun:моєї|Моєї}} руки цю чашу, повну вина {{deity_pronoun:мого|Мого}} гніву, і напій нею всі народи, до яких {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} посилаю тебе.
uk.R: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}, Бог Ізраїлю, сказав мені: «Ось чаша в {{deity_pronoun:моїй|Моїй}} руці. Вона повна вина, і це вино — {{deity_pronoun:мій|Мій}} гнів. Візьми її. Тоді йди до всіх народів, до яких {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} посилаю тебе, і змуси їх пити з неї.

decisions.choice: the cup of the wine of wrath: God's judgment pictured as a cup the nations must drink
decisions.reason: The cup that makes those who drink it reel is a common picture of God's judgment: Psalm 75:9; Isaiah 51:17, 22; Habakkuk 2:16; Lamentations 4:21; Ezekiel 23:31-33. Jeremiah returns to it in 49:12 and 51:7, where Babylon itself is the cup in God's hand. Revelation takes it up in the "wine of God's wrath" (Revelation 14:10; 16:19).

decisions.choice: the wine, the wrath: wine that is God's wrath
decisions.reason: The two nouns stand side by side, "the wine, the wrath". The second explains the first: the wine is God's anger. It is not wine poured out because of wrath, but wrath itself given as drink.

decisions.choice: take ... and make them drink: a prophetic sign, whose manner is not described
decisions.reason: The text does not say whether Jeremiah carried a cup to the kings of all these nations, saw it in a vision, or acted it out in Jerusalem before their envoys (compare 27:2-3). What matters is that his word carries God's judgment to the nations, as his call said (1:10).

decisions.choice: filled with the wine of my wrath (B); the wine is my anger (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "my" because the cup is from God's hand and the wrath is his. Readable unfolds the picture in short sentences. The LORD's words to Jeremiah open a quotation that closes at the end of verse 16.

decisions.choice: la copa del vino de la ira
decisions.reason: God's judgment pictured as a cup (meaning decision m1) is "copa" at every level, the everyday Spanish word for a drinking cup.

decisions.choice: kikombe cha divai ya ghadhabu
decisions.reason: "Kikombe" as the cup of judgment, the word the New Testament uses for the cup Jesus must drink (Matthew 26:39), so the picture is recognisable.

decisions.choice: "Ainsi me parla le SEIGNEUR" (L); "Le SEIGNEUR me dit ceci" (B); "Voici ce que le SEIGNEUR m'a dit" (R)
decisions.reason: The formula in Jeremiah's own narrative frame, as the terms note sets it.

decisions.choice: "chén rượu thịnh nộ"
decisions.reason: "Chén" is the cup of judgment and of the Lord's Supper in the published New Testament, so the picture of meaning decision m1 keeps its familiar word.

decisions.choice: "진노의 포도주가 담긴 잔"
decisions.reason: God's judgment as a cup of wine the nations must drink (meaning decision m1); "진노" is the word for God's wrath used in this book.

decisions.choice: o cálice (every level)
decisions.reason: The cup of God's judgment (m1) is "o cálice", the word Psalm 75:9 and Isaiah 51:17 use for it in Portuguese, and Matthew 26:39 for the cup Jesus drinks; God speaks to Jeremiah with "tu".

decisions.choice: "የቁጣ ወይን ጽዋ" (the cup of the wine of wrath)
decisions.reason: "ጽዋ" is the cup of the Psalms and of the Prophets' cup of judgment; Revelation 14:10, which echoes this picture, has "ዋንጫ" in the Amharic New Testament, but it does not quote this verse.

decisions.choice: "чаша" for the cup of wrath, "напій нею" (L, B) and "змуси їх пити з неї" (R), through 25:15-29
decisions.reason: "Чаша" is the usual word for a cup of judgment and stays the same in each verse of the passage.

decisions.choice: क्रोध की मदिरा का कटोरा
decisions.reason: The cup of the wine of wrath keeps कटोरा for the cup, as Isaiah 51:17, 22 have "उनके क्रोध का कटोरा" in this translation, and मदिरा for the wine. The same words run through the scene (25:15-28).

decisions.choice: чаша вина ярости (L); чаша, полная вина моей ярости (B); вино — мой гнев (R)
decisions.reason: The cup is God's judgment that the nations must drink; "ярость" keeps the heat of the Hebrew word at Literal and Balanced, and Readable unfolds the picture as the English does.

decisions.choice: kos hayyayin hachemah "憤りのぶどう酒の杯" (L), "憤りのぶどう酒で満ちた杯" (B), R in three sentences as the English R; chemah "憤り" (L, B), "怒り" (R).
decisions.reason: m1, m2: wine that is God's wrath; Jeremiah narrates (plain L, B; です・ます R) and God commands him (〜なさい).

records.literal_gloss: And they will drink and they will reel and they will act madly because of the sword that I [am] sending among them.

en.L: And they will drink, and they will reel and act like madmen because of the sword that I am sending among them."
en.B: When they drink, they will stagger and lose their minds because of the sword I am sending among them."
en.R: When they drink it, they will stagger around and act as if they were crazy. This will happen because of the war I am sending among them."

es.L: Y beberán, y se tambalearán y enloquecerán a causa de la espada que yo envío entre ellas».

es.R: Cuando la beban, se tambalearán y actuarán como locos. Esto pasará por causa de la guerra que voy a enviar entre ellas».

fr.L: Et ils boiront, et ils tituberont, et ils perdront la raison à cause de l’épée que j’envoie parmi eux. »

vi.L: Chúng sẽ uống, rồi lảo đảo và hóa điên cuồng vì cớ gươm mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sai đến giữa chúng."
vi.B: Khi uống rồi, chúng sẽ lảo đảo và mất trí vì cớ gươm {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sai đến giữa chúng."
vi.R: Khi uống chén ấy, họ sẽ đi lảo đảo và hành động như người điên. Việc ấy sẽ xảy ra vì chiến tranh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sai đến giữa họ."

ko.L: 그들이 마시고, 내가 그들 가운데로 보내는 칼 때문에 비틀거리며 미친 듯이 행동할 것이다."
ko.B: 그들은 그것을 마시고, 내가 그들 가운데로 보내는 칼 때문에 비틀거리며 정신을 잃을 것이다."
ko.R: 그들은 그 잔을 마시고 비틀거리며 미친 사람처럼 행동할 것이다. 내가 그들 가운데로 보내는 전쟁 때문에 그렇게 될 것이다."

pt.L: E eles beberão, e cambalearão, e enlouquecerão por causa da espada que estou enviando entre eles."
pt.B: Quando beberem, vão cambalear e perder o juízo por causa da espada que estou enviando entre eles."
pt.R: Quando beberem, vão cambalear e agir como loucos. Isso vai acontecer por causa da guerra que estou mandando para o meio deles."

hi.L: और वे पीएँगे, और लड़खड़ाएँगे और पागलों जैसा व्यवहार करेंगे, उस तलवार के कारण जो मैं उनके बीच भेज रहा हूँ।"

ru.L: И будут пить, и будут шататься и безумствовать от меча, который {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} посылаю между ними.»
ru.B: Когда они выпьют, они будут шататься и потеряют рассудок от меча, который {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} посылаю на них.»
ru.R: Когда они выпьют, они будут шататься и вести себя как сумасшедшие. Это будет из-за войны, которую {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} посылаю на них.»

ja.L: 彼らは飲み、よろめき、狂ったようになる。わたしが彼らの間に送る剣のゆえに。」
ja.B: 彼らはそれを飲むと、よろめき、正気を失う。わたしが彼らの間に送る剣のためだ。」

uk.L: І вони питимуть, і хитатимуться, і шаленітимуть через меч, який {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} посилаю між них».
uk.B: Коли вони питимуть, то хитатимуться і втратять розум через меч, який {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} посилаю між них».
uk.R: Коли вони питимуть з неї, то хитатимуться і поводитимуться, наче божевільні. Це станеться через війну, яку {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} посилаю між них».

decisions.choice: reel and act madly: stagger and lose control, like drunken people
decisions.reason: The first verb means to sway back and forth; the second, to act like one out of his mind (51:7). The nations are thrown into helpless confusion.

decisions.choice: because of the sword: the picture of the cup is explained by real war
decisions.reason: The drunkenness stands for the effect of the war God sends: armies broken and peoples in panic. Verse 27 repeats the phrase.

decisions.choice: war
decisions.reason: Readable says "war" for "the sword", as the set wording for sword, famine and pestilence does in Jeremiah.

sw.R: Basi nilikichukua kikombe kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Nikayanywesha mataifa yote aliyonituma kwao. Hawa ndio waliokinywa:

vi.L: Vậy tôi lấy chén khỏi tay {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và cho mọi dân tộc mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã sai tôi đến uống [chén ấy]:
vi.B: Vậy tôi lấy chén khỏi tay {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và cho mọi dân tộc {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã sai tôi đến uống chén ấy:
vi.R: Vậy tôi lấy chén ấy từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Tôi bắt mọi dân tộc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sai tôi đến phải uống chén ấy. Đây là những dân đã uống chén ấy:

ko.L: 그래서 내가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 손에서 그 잔을 받아, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 보내신 모든 민족에게 [그것을] 마시게 했다.
ko.B: 그래서 나는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 손에서 그 잔을 받아, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 보내신 모든 민족에게 그것을 마시게 했다.
ko.R: 그래서 나는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 그 잔을 받았다. 그리고 그분께서 나를 보내신 모든 민족에게 그것을 마시게 했다. 그것을 마신 이들은 다음과 같다.

pt.L: E tomei o cálice da mão {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} e [o] dei a beber a todas as nações às quais {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me enviou:
pt.B: Então tomei o cálice da mão {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} e o dei a beber a todas as nações às quais {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha me enviado:
pt.R: Então peguei o cálice que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me deu. Fiz beber dele todas as nações às quais {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me enviou. Estas são as que beberam:

am.L: ጽዋውንም {{divine_name:ከእግዚአብሔር|ከያህዌ}} እጅ ወሰድኩ፤ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ወደ እነርሱ የላከኝንም ሕዝቦች ሁሉ አጠጣኋቸው፦
am.B: ስለዚህ ጽዋውን {{divine_name:ከእግዚአብሔር|ከያህዌ}} እጅ ወሰድኩ፤ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ወደ እነርሱ የላከኝን ሕዝቦች ሁሉ አጠጣኋቸው፦
am.R: ስለዚህ ጽዋውን {{divine_name:ከእግዚአብሔር|ከያህዌ}} ወሰድኩ። እርሱ ወደ እነርሱ የላከኝን ሕዝቦች ሁሉ ከእርሱ አጠጣኋቸው። የጠጡትም እነዚህ ናቸው፦

hi.L: और मैंने {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के हाथ से कटोरा लिया, और उन सब जातियों को [उसे] पिलाया जिनके पास {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने मुझे भेजा:
hi.B: तब मैंने {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के हाथ से वह कटोरा लिया, और उन सब देशों को उसे पिलाया जिनके पास {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने मुझे भेजा था:
hi.R: तब मैंने {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} से वह कटोरा ले लिया। जिन जिन देशों के पास उन्होंने मुझे भेजा, मैंने उन सब को उसमें से पिलाया। जिन्होंने उसे पिया, वे ये हैं:

ru.L: И взял я чашу из руки {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}, и напоил все народы, к которым послал меня {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}:
ru.B: Я взял чашу из руки {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}} и напоил ею все народы, к которым {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} послал меня:
ru.R: И я взял чашу у {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}. Я дал выпить из неё всем народам, к которым {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} меня послал. Вот те, кто пил из неё:

ja.L: そこで、わたしは{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の手から杯を受け取り、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}がわたしを遣わされたすべての国々に飲ませた。
ja.B: そこで、わたしは{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の手から杯を受け取り、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}がわたしを遣わされたすべての国々に、それを飲ませた。
ja.R: そこで、わたしは{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}から杯を受け取りました。そして、その方がわたしを遣わされたすべての国々に、それを飲ませました。それを飲んだのは、次の者たちです。

uk.L: І я взяв чашу з руки {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}} і напоїв усі народи, до яких {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}} послав мене:
uk.B: Тож я взяв чашу з руки {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}} і напоїв нею всі народи, до яких {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}} мене послав:
uk.R: Тож я взяв чашу від {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}}. Я змусив пити з неї всі народи, до яких {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} мене послав. Ось ті, хто пив з неї:

decisions.choice: I took ... and made them drink: Jeremiah does as he is told
decisions.reason: The account uses the same verbs as the command in verse 15. The list of those who drank follows in verses 18-26, one long sentence.

decisions.choice: a colon at the end of the verse, with the list in verses 18-26
decisions.reason: The list of nations is the object of "made ... drink". Literal and Balanced end each verse of the list with a comma or semicolon; Readable supplies "These are the ones who drank it" and gives each group a short sentence.

decisions.choice: Verse 17 closed as a sentence, and the list of verses 18-26 set as a series of noun phrases
decisions.reason: Korean puts the verb last; a single sentence would have to hold its verb back to verse 26. The list is set as Korean sets a roll of names, each verse ending in a comma, as in the English Literal and Balanced; Readable makes each verse a sentence, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: The verb "飲ませた" is fronted here, and the list of 25:18-26 follows: at L as noun phrases joined by 、 (the verb supplied [飲ませた] at the end, 25:26), at B with "…にも飲ませた" in each verse, at R with "…も飲みました", as the English R "So did …".
decisions.reason: A Japanese verb comes last, and the list runs over nine verses; this keeps each verse's names after its own marker (ISA-1 rule for long lists).

source.text: אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ וְאֶת־עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וְאֶת־מְלָכֶ֖יהָ אֶת־שָׂרֶ֑יהָ לָתֵ֨ת אֹתָ֜ם לְחָרְבָּ֧ה לְשַׁמָּ֛ה לִשְׁרֵקָ֥ה וְלִקְלָלָ֖ה כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Jerusalem and [the] cities of Judah and its kings, its princes, to make them a ruin, a horror, a hissing and a curse, as the day this;

en.L: Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, and its kings [and] its princes, to make them a ruin, a horror, a hissing and a curse, as [it is] this day;
en.B: Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, its kings and its officials, to make them a ruin, a horror, an object of scorn and a curse, as they are today;
en.R: Jerusalem and the towns of Judah drank it, with their kings and leaders. It made them a ruin, a horror, something people mock and a curse, as they are today.

es.L: a Jerusalén y a las ciudades de Judá, y a sus reyes [y] a sus príncipes, para ponerlos por ruina, por horror, por burla y por maldición, como [sucede] hoy;
es.B: a Jerusalén y a las ciudades de Judá, a sus reyes y a sus jefes, para convertirlos en una ruina, un horror, un objeto de burla y una maldición, como lo son hoy;
es.R: Jerusalén y las ciudades de Judá la bebieron, junto con sus reyes y dirigentes. Eso los convirtió en una ruina, un horror, algo de lo que la gente se burla y una maldición, como lo son hoy.

fr.L: Jérusalem et les villes de Juda, ses rois [et] ses princes, pour en faire une ruine, une horreur, un objet de sifflements et une malédiction, comme [c’est le cas] aujourd’hui ;
fr.B: Jérusalem et les villes de Juda, ses rois et ses chefs, pour en faire une ruine, un objet d’horreur et de moquerie, et une malédiction, comme on le voit aujourd’hui ;
fr.R: Jérusalem et les villes de Juda en ont bu, avec leurs rois et leurs chefs. Cela en a fait une ruine, une horreur, quelque chose dont les gens se moquent et une malédiction, comme on le voit aujourd’hui.

sw.L: Yerusalemu na miji ya Yuda, na wafalme wake [na] wakuu wake, ili kuwafanya kuwa magofu, kitisho, [kitu cha] kuzomewa na laana, kama [ilivyo] siku hii ya leo;
sw.B: Yerusalemu na miji ya Yuda, wafalme wake na maafisa wake, ili kuwafanya kuwa magofu, kitisho, kitu cha kudharauliwa na laana, kama walivyo leo;
sw.R: Yerusalemu na miji ya Yuda walikinywa, pamoja na wafalme wao na viongozi wao. Kiliwafanya kuwa magofu, kitisho, kitu ambacho watu hukidhihaki na laana, kama walivyo leo.

vi.L: Giê-ru-sa-lem và các thành của Giu-đa, các vua [và] các quan trưởng của nó, để làm cho chúng thành nơi hoang tàn, một điều kinh hoàng, một tiếng huýt sáo và một sự rủa sả, như [hiện có] ngày nay;
vi.B: Giê-ru-sa-lem và các thành của Giu-đa, các vua và các quan chức của nó, để làm cho chúng thành nơi hoang tàn, một điều kinh hoàng, một mối nhạo báng và một lời nguyền rủa, như ngày nay;
vi.R: Giê-ru-sa-lem và các thành của Giu-đa đã uống, cùng với các vua và các nhà lãnh đạo của chúng. Chén ấy làm cho chúng thành nơi hoang tàn, một nơi đáng sợ, một chỗ người ta chế giễu và một lời nguyền rủa, như chúng ngày nay.

ko.L: 예루살렘과 유다의 성읍들과 그 왕들과 그 고관들, 곧 그들을 폐허와 공포와 휘파람거리와 저주가 되게 하려는 것이니, 오늘과 같다.
ko.B: 예루살렘과 유다의 성읍들과 그 왕들과 관리들이다. 그들을 폐허와 공포의 대상과 비웃음거리와 저주거리가 되게 하려는 것이니, 오늘 보는 바와 같다.
ko.R: 예루살렘과 유다의 성읍들이 왕들과 지도자들과 함께 그것을 마셨다. 그래서 그들은 오늘처럼 폐허가 되고, 끔찍한 곳, 사람들이 비웃는 곳, 저주받은 곳이 되었다.

pt.L: Jerusalém e as cidades de Judá, e os seus reis [e] os seus príncipes, para fazer deles uma ruína, um horror, um assobio e uma maldição, como [é] neste dia;
pt.B: Jerusalém e as cidades de Judá, os seus reis e os seus oficiais, para fazer deles uma ruína, um horror, um objeto de zombaria e uma maldição, como estão hoje;
pt.R: Jerusalém e as cidades de Judá beberam, com os seus reis e os seus líderes. Isso fez delas uma ruína, um horror, algo de que as pessoas zombam e uma maldição, como estão hoje.

am.L: ኢየሩሳሌምንና የይሁዳን ከተሞች፣ ነገሥታቷንና አለቆቿን፣ ፍርስራሽና ድንጋጤ፣ ማፏጫና እርግማን አደርጋቸው ዘንድ፣ እንደ ዛሬው ቀን፤
am.B: ኢየሩሳሌምንና የይሁዳን ከተሞች፣ ነገሥታቷንና ባለ ሥልጣናቷን፣ ዛሬ እንደሚታየው ፍርስራሽ፣ የድንጋጤና የመዘባበቻ ምልክት፣ መራገሚያም አደርጋቸው ዘንድ፤
am.R: ኢየሩሳሌምና የይሁዳ ከተሞች ከነገሥታታቸውና ከመሪዎቻቸው ጋር ጠጡት። ፍርስራሽ፣ አስደንጋጭ ነገር፣ ሰዎች የሚሳለቁበትና የሚራገሙበት አደረጋቸው፤ ዛሬም እንዲሁ ናቸው።

hi.L: यरूशलेम और यहूदा के नगरों को, और उसके राजाओं [और] उसके हाकिमों को, कि उन्हें खंडहर, भय का कारण, सीटी का विषय और शाप बना दूँ, जैसा आज के दिन [है];
hi.B: यरूशलेम और यहूदा के नगरों को, उसके राजाओं और उसके अधिकारियों को, कि उन्हें खंडहर, भय का कारण, उपहास का विषय और शाप बना दूँ, जैसे वे आज हैं;
hi.R: यरूशलेम और यहूदा के नगरों ने, और उनके राजाओं और अगुवों ने उसे पिया। उसने उन्हें खंडहर बना दिया, एक भयानक दृश्य, जिसका लोग मज़ाक़ उड़ाते हैं और जिसका नाम शाप देने में लिया जाता है, जैसे वे आज हैं।

ru.L: Иерусалим, и города Иуды, и его царей, его князей, чтобы сделать их развалинами, ужасом, посмеянием и проклятием, как [это] в этот день;
ru.B: Иерусалим и города Иуды, его царей и его вельмож, чтобы сделать их развалинами, ужасом, предметом насмешек и проклятием, как это и есть сегодня;
ru.R: Пили Иерусалим и города Иуды вместе с их царями и начальниками. Чаша сделала их развалинами, ужасом, тем, над чем люди смеются, и проклятием. Так и есть сегодня.

ja.L: エルサレムとユダの町々、その王たち、その長たちに[飲ませ]、彼らを廃墟とし、恐怖とし、あざけりの口笛とし、呪いとした。今日のとおりである。
ja.B: エルサレムとユダの町々、その王たちと高官たちに飲ませ、彼らを廃墟とし、恐怖とあざけりの的とし、呪いとした。今日見るとおりである。
ja.R: エルサレムとユダの町々が、その王たちや指導者たちと一緒に飲みました。そのため、そこは廃墟となり、恐ろしい所となり、人々があざける所となり、のろいの言葉に使われるようになりました。今日、そのとおりになっています。

uk.L: Єрусалим і міста Юди, і його царів, [і] його князів, щоб зробити їх руїною, жахом, посвистом і прокляттям, як [є] цього дня;
uk.B: Єрусалим і міста Юдеї, її царів і її урядників, щоб зробити їх руїною, жахом, предметом зневаги і прокляттям, як воно і є сьогодні;
uk.R: Пили з неї Єрусалим і міста Юдеї разом зі своїми царями і провідниками. Вона зробила їх руїною, жахом, тим, з чого люди глузують, і прокляттям, як воно і є сьогодні.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem first: judgment begins with God's own city
decisions.reason: The list starts with Jerusalem and Judah before it turns to the nations. Verse 29 gives the reason: if God begins with the city called by his name, the other nations cannot escape.

decisions.choice: a ruin, a horror, a hissing and a curse: a place destroyed, appalling, mocked and used as an example in curses
decisions.reason: As in verse 9 and 19:8. To become "a curse" is for one's name to be used when people curse, as in "may you be like them" (24:9; 29:22).

decisions.choice: as it is this day: the words look back on the judgment as already come
decisions.reason: The phrase means that the ruin had happened by the time these words were written down, which fits the book being gathered after Jerusalem fell. The Greek translation lacks it (see the note at 1:1; this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: princes (L), officials (B), leaders (R); a hissing (L), an object of scorn (B), something people mock (R)
decisions.reason: The set wording for *sar* and for this list. Readable supplies "drank it" and "It made them" to keep the list in short sentences.

decisions.choice: "princes" (L); "chefs" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Sar as 2 Kings 24:12-14 in French.

decisions.choice: князья (L); вельможи (B); начальники (R)
decisions.reason: The king's officials (sarim) take the forms settled for Ezra and Jeremiah 1:18.

decisions.choice: sareha "その長たち" (L), "高官たち" (B), "指導者たち" (R); lechorbah leshammah lishreqah veliqlalah "廃墟、恐怖、あざけりの口笛、呪い" (L), as 25:9.
decisions.reason: JER forms; kayyom hazzeh "今日のとおりである" (m3, footnoted).

source.text: אֶת־פַּרְעֹ֧ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֛יִם וְאֶת־עֲבָדָ֥יו וְאֶת־שָׂרָ֖יו וְאֶת־כָּל־עַמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Pharaoh king of Egypt and his servants and his princes and all his people,

en.L: Pharaoh king of Egypt, and his servants, and his princes, and all his people,
en.B: Pharaoh king of Egypt, his servants, his officials and all his people,
en.R: Pharaoh king of Egypt drank it, with his officials, his leaders and all his people.

es.L: al faraón, rey de Egipto, y a sus siervos, y a sus príncipes, y a todo su pueblo,
es.B: al faraón, rey de Egipto, a sus servidores, a sus jefes y a todo su pueblo,
es.R: El faraón, rey de Egipto, la bebió, junto con sus funcionarios, sus jefes y todo su pueblo.

fr.L: le pharaon, roi d’Égypte, et ses serviteurs, et ses princes, et tout son peuple,

decisions.choice: Pharaoh king of Egypt: Pharaoh Neco, the king of that time
decisions.reason: In 605 BC the pharaoh was Neco II, who had killed Josiah (2 Kings 23:29) and whose army Nebuchadrezzar defeated that year at Carchemish (46:2). Egypt heads the foreign nations, from the south, and the list moves north and east to Babylon at the end.

decisions.choice: his servants and his princes: the members of his court and his high officials
decisions.reason: "Servants" here are a king's courtiers and officials, not household slaves.

decisions.choice: servants and princes (L); servants and officials (B); officials and leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The set wording for a king's servants and for *sar*. Balanced keeps "servants" so that the two words stay distinct.

decisions.choice: Faraó, without the article
decisions.reason: As the Old Testament terms set it, "Faraó" without the article where the English says "Pharaoh" as a name.

decisions.choice: दास और हाकिम (L); दास और अधिकारी (B); अधिकारी और अगुवे (R)
decisions.reason: A king's servants and princes keep the wording of 2 Kings 24:12 at Literal, दास and हाकिम; Balanced says दास and अधिकारी, the book's Balanced word for sarim (1:18), so the two words stay apart; Readable says अधिकारी and अगुवे, as the English Readable says "officials and leaders".

decisions.choice: рабы (L); приближённые (B, R)
decisions.reason: A king's servants take the forms of 2 Samuel: "рабы" at Literal and "приближённые" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: Par'oh "ファラオ"; 'avadav "その家臣たち" (every level, as 22:2); sarav "その長たち" (L), "高官たち" (B), "指導者たち" (R).
decisions.reason: m2: his court and his high officials.

records.literal_gloss: and all the mixed people, and all [the] kings of [the] land of the Uz, and all [the] kings of [the] land of [the] Philistines, and Ashkelon and Gaza and Ekron and [the] remnant of Ashdod;

en.L: and all the mixed people, and all the kings of the land of Uz, and all the kings of the land of the Philistines: Ashkelon and Gaza and Ekron and the remnant of Ashdod;
en.B: all the foreign peoples there; all the kings of the land of Uz; all the kings of the land of the Philistines, of Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron and what is left of Ashdod;
en.R: So did all the foreigners who lived in Egypt, and all the kings of the land of Uz. So did all the kings of the Philistines, in the cities of Ashkelon, Gaza and Ekron, and the people left in Ashdod.

es.L: y a toda la mezcla de pueblos, y a todos los reyes de la tierra de Uz, y a todos los reyes de la tierra de los filisteos: Ascalón, Gaza, Ecrón y el remanente de Asdod;

es.R: También la bebieron todos los extranjeros que vivían en Egipto, y todos los reyes de la tierra de Uz. También la bebieron todos los reyes de los filisteos, en las ciudades de Ascalón, Gaza y Ecrón, y la gente que quedaba en Asdod.

fr.L: et tout le peuple mêlé, et tous les rois du pays d’Outs, et tous les rois du pays des Philistins : Ashqelôn, Gaza, Ekron et le reste d’Ashdod ;
fr.B: tous les peuples étrangers qui vivaient là ; tous les rois du pays d’Outs ; tous les rois du pays des Philistins, d’Ashqelôn, de Gaza, d’Ekron et de ce qui reste d’Ashdod ;

am.R: በግብፅ የሚኖሩ ባዕዳን ሁሉና የዑፅ ምድር ነገሥታት ሁሉ እንዲሁ ጠጡት። በአስቀሎን፣ በጋዛና በአቃሮን ከተሞች ያሉ የፍልስጥኤማውያን ነገሥታት ሁሉና በአዛጦን የቀሩት ሰዎችም እንዲሁ ጠጡት።

ru.L: и весь смешанный народ, и всех царей земли Уц, и всех царей земли филистимлян: и Аскалон, и Газу, и Аккарон, и остаток Азота;

ru.R: Пили и все чужеземцы, жившие в Египте, и все цари земли Уц. Пили все цари филистимлян в городах Аскалоне, Газе и Аккароне и люди, оставшиеся в Азоте.

ja.L: すべての混じり合った民、ウツの地のすべての王たち、ペリシテ人の地のすべての王たち、すなわちアシュケロン、ガザ、エクロン、アシュドドの残りの者、
